# Mathematics: Chapter 8 — Introduction to Trigonometry — Formula Sheet

## Trigonometric Ratios

### Definitions in a Right Triangle
For a right-angled triangle $ABC$ with $\angle B = 90^\circ$ and acute angle $A$:

\[
\sin A = \frac{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AC}
\]

\[
\cos A = \frac{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{AB}{AC}
\]

\[
\tan A = \frac{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A}{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A} = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{\sin A}{\cos A}
\]

\[
\csc A = \frac{1}{\sin A} = \frac{AC}{BC}, \quad \sec A = \frac{1}{\cos A} = \frac{AC}{AB}, \quad \cot A = \frac{1}{\tan A} = \frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}
\]

## Trigonometric Ratios of Specific Angles

| Ratio | $0^\circ$ | $30^\circ$ | $45^\circ$ | $60^\circ$ | $90^\circ$ |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $\sin \theta$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ | $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $1$ |
| $\cos \theta$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $0$ |
| $\tan \theta$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ | $1$ | $\sqrt{3}$ | Not defined |
| $\csc \theta$ | Not defined | $2$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ | $1$ |
| $\sec \theta$ | $1$ | $\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $2$ | Not defined |
| $\cot \theta$ | Not defined | $\sqrt{3}$ | $1$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ | $0$ |

## Trigonometric Identities

### Fundamental Pythagorean Identities
Valid for all acute angles $0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ$:

\[
\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1
\]

\[
1 + \tan^2 \theta = \sec^2 \theta \iff \sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta = 1 \quad (0^\circ \le \theta < 90^\circ)
\]

\[
1 + \cot^2 \theta = \csc^2 \theta \iff \csc^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta = 1 \quad (0^\circ < \theta \le 90^\circ)
\]

## Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

\[
\sin(90^\circ - A) = \cos A, \quad \cos(90^\circ - A) = \sin A
\]
\[
\tan(90^\circ - A) = \cot A, \quad \cot(90^\circ - A) = \tan A
\]
\[
\sec(90^\circ - A) = \csc A, \quad \csc(90^\circ - A) = \sec A
\]

> **Remember:** $\sin \theta$ and $\cos \theta$ never exceed $1$: $0 \le \sin \theta \le 1$ and $0 \le \cos \theta \le 1$ for acute $\theta$.
